title: Microsoft Copilot: CSV and TSV files as knowledge sources in Copilot Notebooks
summary: The briefing passes: the rollout, automatic enablement and administrator recommendations match Microsoft's notice. Microsoft Learn supports the creation policy and its preview automation, and the briefing accurately reports the differing licensing wording.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends notifying users who work with structured data about CSV and TSV references.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no page describing CSV and TSV references in Copilot Notebooks.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Notebooks" "CSV" "TSV"; "Copilot Notebooks" "CSV". Read cpcn-admin-configuration, cpcn-requirements, cpcn-storage and release-notes; searched release-notes for CSV, TSV and 569210. No matching feature description found.

claims.claim: Disabling creation does not delete existing Copilot Pages or Notebooks.
claims.quote: Existing Copilot Pages and Notebooks aren't deleted.

claims.claim: Files added to Notebooks remain available in their original OneDrive and SharePoint storage locations when creation is disabled.
claims.quote: Original storage locations: Files added to Notebooks remain available in OneDrive and SharePoint where they're stored

claims.claim: The sources describe no sign-in change for this CSV and TSV enhancement.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Notebooks CSV TSV sign-in roles connectors autonomous behavior. Read roadmap record, MC1519841 and cited Learn pages; no sign-in change for these file types was described. Search results concerned other products or existing connectors.

claims.claim: The sources describe no role change introduced by CSV and TSV references.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Notebooks CSV TSV sign-in roles connectors autonomous behavior. Read roadmap record, MC1519841, cpcn-admin-configuration and utcm-copilot-resources; roles documented for existing policy automation are not changes introduced by these file types.

claims.claim: The sources describe additional file types, not a new connector or agent.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Notebooks CSV TSV sign-in roles connectors autonomous behavior. Read roadmap record and MC1519841; search returned CSV connector documentation, but not a connector or agent introduced by Notebook CSV/TSV references.

claims.claim: No autonomous behaviour is described for this enhancement; the described workflow uses user-added references to generate responses.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Notebooks CSV TSV sign-in roles connectors autonomous behavior. Read roadmap record, MC1519841 and cited Learn pages; the feature description covers adding knowledge sources and generating responses, not autonomous actions.

claims.claim: Learn lists a creation setting and a code-preview setting as the two Cloud Policy settings checked by Copilot Pages and Notebooks.
claims.quote: Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks check the following Cloud Policy settings: Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks; Enable code previews for AI-generated content in Microsoft Copilot Chat and Copilot Pages

claims.claim: Neither of those documented Cloud Policy settings is CSV- or TSV-specific.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Notebooks" "TSV" "policy". Read both settings and their Enabled, Disabled and Not configured descriptions in cpcn-admin-configuration, plus copilotpagesnotebooks in utcm-copilot-resources; neither mentions CSV or TSV.

claims.claim: Disabling creation hides the Notebooks module in the Microsoft Copilot app for affected users.
claims.quote: The Pages module is visible in the Microsoft Copilot app, but the Notebooks module is hidden, preventing users from accessing existing Notebooks through the Copilot App.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents Copilot policy TCM automation as preview using Microsoft Graph beta.
claims.quote: This article lists the Copilot resource types supported in preview for monitoring and snapshots through the Tenant Configuration Management (TCM) APIs in Microsoft Graph beta. These resources also support remediation and applyOnce.

claims.claim: The monitor's mode=applyOnce applies a desired-state baseline once.
claims.quote: applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode. ... mode | monitorMode | The monitor mode. The possible values are: monitorOnly, applyOnce, unknownFutureValue.

claims.claim: The baseline resourceType for this setting is microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks.
claims.quote: "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks"

claims.claim: The baseline uses resourceVersion 1.
claims.quote: "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks", "resourceVersion": 1

claims.claim: The baseline properties.value value 0 disables the setting.
claims.quote: value | Write | String | Allows or prevents creating and viewing Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Copilot Actions. 0 disables the setting; 1 enables the setting.

claims.claim: The baseline properties.value value 1 enables the setting.
claims.quote: 0 disables the setting; 1 enables the setting. ... "properties": { "value": "1" }

claims.claim: TCM supports these Copilot settings only in tenant-level policies in Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.
claims.quote: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: The target setting must not be configured in any group-level policy for TCM automation to work.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.

claims.claim: The calling app needs delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All to create an applyOnce monitor.
claims.quote: Creating an applyOnce monitor supports delegated permissions only. In addition to the calling app's delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All permission

claims.claim: The TCM service principal needs delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite for applyOnce.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, grant it the CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite delegated permission.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is the role required for the signed-in user performing this preview policy automation.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, AI Administrator is the least-privileged Microsoft Entra role for the signed-in user. This role requirement applies to the user, not to the TCM service principal.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph beta APIs are not supported for production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.
